title: Complete multifunction mechanical alarm clock task suite
goal: Verify the complete twin-bell mechanical alarm clock through authored three-hand timekeeping, manual time setting, independently powered alarm motion, hour-hand alarm-target setting, and selected-position alarm triggering.

profiles.title: Complete multifunction twin-bell clock
profiles.description: The timekeeping barrel owns all three hands, the rear setting input acts through the setting clutch, the hour hand sets the dedicated alarm target through its clutch, and a mechanically separate alarm barrel owns the alarm cam and hammer.

scenarios.title: Run and compare the three-hand clock train
execution_requirements: Drive only the authored timekeeping input and preserve separate traces for the hour, minute, and second hand shafts.
Bind each angular-ratio criterion to its declared numerator and denominator before execution.
Preserve physical and ideal-reference evidence for the same frozen input schedule.

scenarios.title: Set the clock through the rear setting input
execution_requirements: Drive only the authored rear setting input through the finite setting clutch.
Evaluate minute-hand setting travel against the corrected 0.2 rad target with 0.02 rad shortfall tolerance.
Audit the wrench path to prove that no hand shaft is directly actuated.

scenarios.title: Ring the twin-bell alarm independently
execution_requirements: Drive only the independent alarm barrel and record the hammer plus all three hand shafts over the same alarm window.
Audit that the hammer is reached through the alarm cam and follower rather than direct hammer actuation.
Measure hand drift from the settled state immediately before alarm actuation.

scenarios.title: Set the alarm target by turning the hour hand
execution_requirements: Drive only the authored hour-hand alarm-setting input through the finite alarm-target clutch.
Record the hour hand and dedicated alarm-target cam over the setting and latch windows.
Audit the wrench path to prove that the alarm-target cam is not directly actuated.

scenarios.title: Trigger the alarm at the selected hand position
execution_requirements: Set the dedicated alarm target through the hour hand, restore the current display, then drive only the timekeeping barrel.
Record target retention, pre-trigger quiet, selected-position arrival, post-trigger hammer motion, and continued timekeeping in separate windows.
Keep the independent alarm barrel, alarm cam, follower, hammer, and three-hand timekeeping train in the same complete multifunction execution.

tasks.title: Verify three-hand timekeeping
tasks.goal: Move the minute hand far enough to observe the clock train while preserving the authored hour-to-minute and second-to-minute ratios and a consistent display direction.

criteria.description: The minute hand travels at least 0.27 rad, with an approved absolute shortfall tolerance of 0.02 rad.
The hour-hand travel divided by the minute-hand travel remains 1/12 within two percent.
The second-hand travel divided by the minute-hand travel remains 60 within two percent.
All three hands use the display direction declared by the frozen shaft bindings.

failure_diagnostics.description: The minute hand did not produce enough observable travel for the approved test window.
At least one measured hand ratio exceeded its approved tolerance.
A hand moved against its frozen display-direction convention.

evidence_obligations: Preserve the bound hour, minute, and second shaft identities with each measured trace.
Evaluate ratios across the shared powered window rather than from unrelated endpoints.
Retain both physical and ideal-reference results and their comparison.

tasks.title: Verify manual time setting
tasks.goal: Move the minute hand through the authored setting clutch without directly actuating any clock hand.

criteria.description: Manual setting moves the minute hand at least 0.2 rad, with an approved absolute shortfall tolerance of 0.02 rad.
The setting input reaches the hands only through the authored setting clutch and gear train.

failure_diagnostics.description: The corrected 0.2 rad manual-setting target was not reached within its approved shortfall tolerance.
A hand shaft was directly driven instead of moving through the setting clutch and clock train.

evidence_obligations: Preserve the setting-input wrench audit and the minute-hand trace.
Evaluate the corrected 0.2 rad target rather than the historical incorrect 0.02 rad binding.
Retain both physical and ideal-reference results and their comparison.

tasks.title: Verify independent twin-bell alarm motion
tasks.goal: Swing the alarm hammer through the independently powered alarm train while all three clock hands remain effectively stationary.

criteria.description: The alarm hammer swings at least 0.08 rad, with an approved absolute shortfall tolerance of 0.01 rad.
The maximum drift of any clock hand during independent alarm actuation is no more than 0.02 rad.
The alarm input reaches the hammer only through the authored alarm cam and follower.

failure_diagnostics.description: The hammer did not reach the approved minimum swing.
At least one hand drifted more than the approved isolation tolerance during alarm actuation.
The hammer was directly driven instead of moving through the isolated alarm mechanism.

evidence_obligations: Record hammer and all three hand traces over an identical alarm window.
Retain the verified independent-alarm-input wrench audit.
Do not substitute evidence from any shared-power or simplified clock topology.

tasks.title: Set alarm time by turning the hour hand
tasks.goal: Turn the hour hand through its finite clutch, make the dedicated alarm-target cam follow the selected position, hold that target after release, and never actuate the target cam directly.

criteria.description: At the latched setting position, the dedicated alarm target differs from the hour-hand selection by no more than 0.0025 rad.
After the hour-hand setting input is released, the dedicated alarm target drifts by no more than 0.0025 rad.
The hour-hand setting input reaches the dedicated alarm-target cam only through the authored finite clutch.

failure_diagnostics.description: The latched alarm target did not match the selected hour-hand position within tolerance.
The alarm target drifted after the setting input was released.
The alarm-target cam was driven directly instead of through the hour-hand clutch.

evidence_obligations: Preserve the hour-hand and alarm-target traces over the setting and latch windows.
Retain the hour-hand input wrench audit and finite-clutch topology evidence.
Bind both latch criteria to the dedicated alarm-target cam from the complete multifunction clock.

tasks.title: Trigger alarm at the selected hand position
tasks.goal: Retain the selected alarm target while the three-hand train advances, remain quiet before the hour hand reaches that target, ring the independent alarm, and continue timekeeping afterward.

criteria.description: At trigger, the running hour hand differs from the retained alarm target by no more than 0.0025 rad.
The selected alarm target drifts by no more than 0.0025 rad while the timekeeping train advances to it.
Before the selected-position trigger, hammer motion is no more than 0.02 rad.
After the selected-position trigger, the hammer swings at least 0.08 rad with an approved 0.01 rad shortfall tolerance.
After the alarm triggers, the minute hand continues timekeeping by at least 0.03 rad.

failure_diagnostics.description: The hour hand did not reach the retained selected target within tolerance.
The selected alarm target moved before trigger.
The hammer moved before the selected-position trigger.
The post-trigger hammer motion did not reach the approved minimum.
The minute hand did not continue by the approved post-trigger amount.

evidence_obligations: Preserve alarm-target, hour-hand, pre-trigger, trigger, and post-trigger windows with unambiguous boundaries.
Record continued timekeeping after trigger; a hammer-only trace is insufficient.
Retain physical and ideal-reference results for the same frozen setting and timekeeping schedule.

source_projects.note: The complete twin-bell mechanical alarm clock is the authoritative source for the five restored tasks: three-hand timekeeping, manual time setting, independently powered alarm motion, hour-hand alarm-target setting, and selected-position alarm triggering.

approval.basis: The user explicitly approved restoring the complete multifunction mechanical alarm clock's original five-task library.
